# England Saw the Final—Then Messi Opened the Door

England were minutes away from the World Cup final.

On 15 July at Atlanta Stadium, England faced Argentina in a 2026 FIFA World Cup semifinal.

The first half ended goalless.

**0-0.**

Then, in the 55th minute, England broke through.

Harry Kane’s long ball started the move. Morgan Rogers sent a low cross in from the right, and Anthony Gordon met it at the far side.

**England 1-0 Argentina.**

That lead lasted for half an hour.

Then, in the 85th minute, Lionel Messi played the ball sideways from a short-corner move. Enzo Fernández struck from outside the penalty area with his right foot.

**1-1.**

Extra time seemed close. But Argentina had one more attack.

Alexis Mac Allister hit the post. Messi recovered the ball and crossed with his right foot toward the far side. Substitute Lautaro Martínez rose to meet it with his head.

It was 90+2—two minutes into second-half stoppage time.

**Argentina 2-1 England.**

Argentina were through to the final. England were heading to the third-place match.

## Two Defining Angles

### Argentina’s pressure showed in one clear number

The score stayed close. The shot count did not.

Argentina had 15 shots. England had five.

The wider statistical picture also favored Argentina. England came close to protecting their lead, but Argentina kept pushing until the final minutes.

### Messi decided the semifinal without scoring

Messi did not score. But he assisted both Argentina goals.

His pass set up Fernández’s equalizer. His cross created Lautaro’s winner.

At 39 years and 21 days, Messi became the oldest outfield player to appear in a World Cup semifinal. FIFA also named him the Superior Player of the Match.

Fernández and Lautaro supplied the finishes. Messi supplied the answers.

## In One Line…

**England could see the final—but in stoppage time, Messi opened the door for Argentina.**
